questions.text: Which exposure category applies to a site located in flat, undeveloped agricultural land with scattered trees?

options.text: Exposure A (smooth terrain)
Exposure B (moderate roughness)
Exposure C (open terrain)
Exposure D (urban development)

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Exposure C is defined for open terrain with occasional obstructions—grassland, scattered trees, and undeveloped land all fall into this category.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A building has a mean roof height of 20 meters and a rectangular plan dimension of 30 m × 40 m. Is this a low-rise building?

options.text: Yes; mean roof height of 20 m satisfies the ≤18 m criterion
No; mean roof height of 20 m exceeds the 18 m limit
Yes; the 30 × 40 m plan is large enough to qualify
Cannot determine without knowing exposure category

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Low-rise requires mean roof height ≤60 ft (18.3 m) AND mean roof height ≤ least horizontal dimension. At 20 m (65.6 ft), this building exceeds the 60 ft limit, so it fails the first condition and is not low-rise.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A building has all external walls fitted with louvers and vents that total 85% of wall area. What is this building classified as?

options.text: Enclosed building
Open building
Partially enclosed building
Semi-enclosed building (non-standard)

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: An open building has all external walls at least 80% open. 85% exceeds the 80% threshold for all walls, so this building is open.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: The basic wind speed V is defined as which of the following?

options.text: The maximum wind gust ever recorded at a site, typically measured during extreme weather events
The 3-second peak gust speed at 10 meters above ground in Exposure C terrain
The average hourly wind velocity measured in open terrain, used for general climatological assessments
The 1-minute sustained wind speed at ground level, often used in maritime and aviation contexts

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Basic wind speed is precisely defined as a 3-second gust speed at 10 m height in Exposure C. This is the reference hazard level used to derive all site-specific and height-adjusted wind pressures.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: An engineer must select a wind load procedure for a 22 m tall industrial building in Exposure B with a 28 m × 28 m square footprint. The measured fundamental frequency is 1.3 Hz. Explain which procedure applies and justify your classification decisions.

options.text: General wind procedure (not low-rise); not low-rise (22 m > 18 m); not flexible (1.3 Hz > 1 Hz and 22 < 4×28=112)
Low-rise procedure; low-rise building; not flexible; all conditions satisfied, including height and frequency parameters
Dynamic procedure; low-rise building but frequency threshold requires dynamic analysis due to specific site conditions
Dynamic procedure; not low-rise; height exceeds 4 × least dimension (22 > 7), necessitating a more complex analysis

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Mean roof height 22 m > 18 m, so NOT low-rise (low-rise requires ≤18 m AND ≤ least dimension). Frequency 1.3 Hz > 1 Hz and height ratio 22 ÷ 28 = 0.79, which is << 4, so NOT flexible. Neither low-rise nor flexible criteria are met, therefore a general procedure (non-simplified) applies; simplified low-rise procedure does not apply.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A tall office tower in an urban downtown area has a height of 85 m and a plan dimension of 25 m × 25 m. Calculate the height-to-least-dimension ratio and determine if flexibility criteria are triggered.

options.text: Ratio 3.4; not flexible (3.4 < 4)
Ratio 3.4; flexible because height exceeds 50 m absolute
Ratio 2.8; requires frequency measurement to determine flexibility
Ratio 3.4; flexible because structure is in Exposure B urban terrain

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Height-to-least-dimension = 85 ÷ 25 = 3.4. The flexible threshold is height > 4 × least dimension, i.e., 100 m. Since 85 m < 100 m, this criterion is not triggered. Unless the natural frequency is < 1 Hz, dynamic analysis is not required by geometry alone.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Which of the following conditions indicates a flexible structure that requires dynamic wind analysis?

options.text: Mean roof height 22 m, plan 30 m × 30 m, natural frequency 1.2 Hz, which is often considered borderline for dynamic analysis
Height 45 m, plan 10 m × 10 m (height = 4.5 × least dimension), natural frequency 0.8 Hz
Height 15 m, plan 40 m × 40 m, natural frequency 1.5 Hz, typically not requiring dynamic analysis unless other factors are present
All buildings over 30 m tall, regardless of frequency, a generalization not supported by structural codes

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Flexible structure is triggered by frequency < 1 Hz OR height > 4 × least horizontal dimension. Option B: frequency 0.8 Hz < 1 Hz ✓ and height 45 m > 4 × 10 m (40 m) ✓. Both conditions are met.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A mixed-use building has a south wall that is 75% open (storefronts) and a north wall that is 92% open (ventilation louvers). What is the building classification?

options.text: Open building
Enclosed building
Partially enclosed building
The classification depends on interior air volume

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Partially enclosed means some external walls are ≥80% open while others are <80% open. South wall 75% < 80% and north wall 92% ≥ 80%. Because not all walls meet the ≥80% criterion, this is partially enclosed.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: The annual probability of exceedance for basic wind speed is 0.02. What does this correspond to?

options.text: A 20-year mean recurrence interval
A 50-year mean recurrence interval
A 100-year mean recurrence interval
A 2% safety factor on all wind pressures

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: An annual probability of 0.02 means a 1 in 50 chance each year, which is equivalent to a 50-year mean recurrence interval (1 ÷ 0.02 = 50).
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A warehouse with a mean roof height of 12 m has a square plan of 50 m × 50 m. Is this a low-rise building?

options.text: Yes; all conditions are satisfied (12 m ≤ 18 m and 12 m ≤ 50 m)
No; the plan is too large for low-rise classification, as it exceeds typical low-rise area limits
No; the height is too close to the 18 m limit, which may require additional structural considerations
Cannot determine without site-specific wind speed data, which could affect structural classification

rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Low-rise requires mean roof height ≤18 m AND ≤ least horizontal dimension. Here: 12 m ≤ 18 m ✓ and 12 m ≤ 50 m ✓. Both conditions are satisfied, so this is a low-rise building.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.
